title: No blame today
hook: entering Mecca, the Prophet echoes Joseph: no blame on you today (Quran 12:92)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Ta'if: offered the mountains against the town, the Prophet hoped for its children instead. Your line was not a curse.

What do you say to the people who pushed you out of your home, on the day you walk back in and could do anything you like to them? The early biographies say the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, faced exactly that. Years after leaving Mecca, he returned with a large following, and the city opened to him. The men who had mocked him, fought him and driven his followers away were gathered, waiting to hear what would happen to them. Tradition says he didn't make up a new answer. He borrowed one from an older story.
screen: `THE CITY THAT DROVE HIM OUT.` → `THE OLD ENEMIES, WAITING.` → `AN ANSWER BORROWED.`

segments.voice: The older story is in the Qur'an's surah of Joseph. His brothers throw him into a well, and he is sold away. Much later he is a powerful man in Egypt, and the brothers come before him needing grain, not knowing who he is. When at last he tells them, they admit they were in the wrong. His answer comes at chapter twelve, verse ninety-two. In paraphrase: there is no blame on you this day; may God forgive you, and he is the most merciful of those who show mercy. No speech about the well. No list of what it cost him. The case is closed in a sentence, and the rest is handed to God. Now the echo. In the sira, when Mecca opened to him, the Prophet asked the Quraysh, his own tribe, what they expected from him. In the telling, they answered that they expected good from a generous brother. And he answered with Joseph's words. Tradition adds that he told them to go; they were free. A grudge is a case kept open, filed and ready to be pulled out. No blame today closes it, on a day you can name. It doesn't say nothing happened; Joseph's brothers knew exactly what happened, and said so. It says the account won't be pressed, and it comes from someone who had every means to press it.
screen: `JOSEPH AND HIS BROTHERS.` · `NO BLAME ON YOU THIS DAY.` · `THE PROPHET BORROWS THE LINE.` · `A CASE CLOSED ON A NAMED DAY.` · then, large: `NO BLAME TODAY.`

segments.voice: Bring up one grudge you've kept open, not the biggest, and picture it as a file on a desk, the evidence all in order. Without arguing the case again, close the cover and quietly name today: not that it didn't happen, only that from today the account isn't pressed. If you pray, you can hand the rest to God in your own tradition's words; if you don't, set the file down and leave it there.
Quraysh. The Prophet's own tribe, asked what they expected from him when Mecca opened to him, and answered with Joseph's words. Today's word.
Your line: the account won't be pressed. If it comes knocking tomorrow, the date still stands. Day nine hundred fifty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims read Joseph's words in surah 12 and tell the sira's account of the Prophet repeating them at Mecca; the phrase is quoted when people are urged to forgive old enemies.

chat.meaning: Qur'an 12:92 gives Joseph's words to his brothers. The sira says the Prophet borrowed them when Mecca opened to him.
